messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Just noticed the usual chatter online — people sharing those odd little memes again. Not sure what’s really shifting, but the quiet ones seem more nervous than usual. Still, the trains are running on time, and nothing’s collapsed yet. Keep your ears open, but don’t say much."
Sender 2: "The air feels different—calmer, but in a way that doesn’t quite sit right. Something’s shifting beneath the surface, and the silence is louder than noise. Be careful how you speak, even to those you trust."
Sender 3: "Just got back from the market—everything’s quiet, prices steady, people talking about next week’s harvest like nothing’s changed. Heard a funny thing on the radio today, repeated the same line twice in a row like it was written wrong—maybe just a glitch, but I swear my phone clicked when it happened. Whatever’s going on, it’s not the kind of thing you’d notice unless you’re already watching."
Sender 4: "The kids’ school’s back to normal, and even the usual quiet has a different feel—like everyone’s holding their breath between beats. Just keep your head down, but don’t look away."
Sender 5: "The air feels thicker than usual — everyone’s watching, but no one’s speaking. Just a quiet sense that things are holding together, for now, but the cracks are starting to show in ways that don’t add up."
Sender 6: "Things feel off—calmer on the surface, but the silence between people’s words is louder than before. I’ve been hearing the same quiet unease from a few others; not panic, just a kind of waiting. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay close."
Sender 7: "Just got word that the new hospital supply issues are spreading — heard a nurse mention they’re already rerouting patients to nearby clinics. Seems like the system’s under pressure, even if things on the surface look calm. Be careful what you share — I’ve noticed a few people suddenly backing off conversations that used to be open."
Sender 8: "Just got back from the market—people are busy fixing up their homes, buying tools, even planting herbs on balconies. Feels like everyone’s quietly betting on the same thing: things are going to keep going, one way or another. Not much to say, but the calm’s starting to feel like a kind of certainty."
Sender 9: "The air feels different—people are talking, even strangers. Something’s shifting, and I’ve seen things that don’t add up. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay sharp."
Sender 10: "The air feels tense but still, like before a storm that might not come. Everyone’s holding their breath—joking to keep from panicking, watching the quiet cracks in the system. Stay sharp, keep it light, but don’t trust the calm."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.

JOIN_PERCENT: 10
